name: KPI Green Energy Ltd
tagline: Renewable-energy IPP/EPC near a 52-week low on margin pressure, sitting on a large land bank and 7 GW order book
business_overview: KPI Green Energy develops and operates renewable energy (solar/wind) projects, both as an independent power producer and EPC contractor, with an installed capacity of 2.5 GW and stated plans to scale beyond 10 GW by 2030.
fundamentals_table: Rs 335.6 - 562.6 (near the low, down ~40% from peak)
fundamentals_narrative: Solid ROE (17.4%) and an aggressive but management-stated growth target (40-50% CAGR to FY30), offset by meaningful leverage (D/E 1.71, typical for a capital-intensive IPP model) and a stock that has corrected ~40% from its peak on margin pressure.
sentiment_summary: Read most recent 50 of 317 posts (single batch, no escalation). Only 2 posts in the fetched window are from the current period (Aug 2026), both raising the same open question: is the recent margin pressure temporary or structural.
community_signal: No trusted-roster users posted in this thread. Ravi_Narsingani (Aug 2026) asked directly whether the margin pressure in the KP group's latest results is a one-off or a continuing trend -- unanswered at time of read. Paulbiplab (Aug 2026) noted the stock is near its 52-week low, down ~40% from peak, but argued execution timing (not fundamentals) explains the decline, pointing to the large land bank and 7 GW order book as still-intact underlying value, and asked the community if anything else is being missed.
bull_case: 7 GW order book and a large land bank provide substantial multi-year growth visibility if execution timing normalizes
17.4% ROE and an explicit 40-50% revenue CAGR target through FY30 are attractive if delivered
Stock has already corrected ~40% from its peak -- some bad news may already be priced in
bear_case: Open, unresolved community question about whether recent margin pressure is temporary or structural -- no clear answer from management yet per the thread
D/E of 1.71 is meaningful leverage for a business whose margins are currently under visible pressure
Stock is near a 52-week low with the community itself uncertain whether this is a buying opportunity or an early warning sign
verdict_headline: Large order book intact, but unresolved margin-pressure questions and real leverage keep this speculative for now
verdict_reasoning: The 7 GW order book and aggressive stated growth target keep this in the 10x-in-2-3-years bucket, and the ~40% correction means downside may be partially priced in already

But this is a live, unresolved community question (temporary vs. structural margin pressure) rather than a confirmed inflection, and the leverage level adds real execution risk if margins stay compressed
Conviction held to low-medium pending clarity on the margin trend in the next 1-2 quarters

four_box.note: 7GW order book + management's 40-50% CAGR-to-FY30 target on a large land bank is a real renewable-IPP tailwind and tam; no distinct moat described for a commodity solar-IPP model — weak; stock near 52-wk low after a ~40% correction with an unresolved community question on whether margin pressure is temporary or structural — valuation weak. D/E 1.71 is meaningful leverage against currently-pressured margins.

market_expectation.implied_growth_cagr: ~13x trailing earnings after a ~40% correction from the peak; against a ~14-16x exit this needs only ~15-20% EPS CAGR, which the 7 GW order book and 40-50% revenue CAGR target would clear easily if margins and leverage hold -- the low multiple prices in the margin-pressure and D/E-1.71 risk
market_expectation.our_fy27_estimate: revenue +35-50% on the order book / land bank; OPM ~32-36%; PAT growth slower than revenue on higher interest as the IPP book scales; FCF remains deeply negative on capex
market_expectation.our_fy28_estimate: continued high revenue growth if execution timing normalises; the swing factor is whether margin pressure is temporary (execution timing) or structural (competitive solar-IPP tariffs)
market_expectation.gap_basis: a ~13x multiple on a 40-50%-growth renewable IPP looks cheap, but ROCE has fallen to ~14%, D/E is 1.71 against currently-pressured margins, FCF is heavily negative on capex, and the community's temporary-vs-structural margin question is unresolved -- the low multiple is compensation for those risks, not a clean mispricing
market_expectation.data_caveat: no broker consensus; implied path is a reverse-P/E estimate + screener.in forward figures + VP thread view

track_record.note: Per screener.in consolidated (FY20-FY26): FY20-FY24 all cleared both bars (revenue +59-180% / ROCE 16-25%); FY25-FY26 ROCE slipped to ~14% on rising leverage (D/E 1.71) and margin pressure even as revenue kept growing 55-69%. Capital-intensive IPP model with deeply negative free cash flow.
